children: The Personal Income and Outlays report for August just dropped.
It includes the PCE price index, also known as the Fed's preferred measure of inflation. Here's what it showed:
The PCE index rose 3.4% over the past year, holding steady from a revised 3.4% rate in July.
It's still significantly above the Fed's 2% inflation target.
On a month-on-month basis, the index ticked up 0.3%.
The core 12-month PCE inflation rate, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, came in at 3%.
